## Several windows at once, without stepping on each other

**Upgrading changes three things you may notice once.**

- **Undo history starts fresh.** Each directory's history is now kept under a name that also
  carries a hash of the full path, so `/home/a-b/c` and `/home/a/b-c` no longer share one. History
  written by 0.4.x is left where it was and not read.
- **Startup only picks up sessions this machine opened.** A new window used to switch into any of
  the account's sessions that was waiting on an answer, including one another window was running.
  It now adopts only sessions whose opening window has ended. Sessions opened before the upgrade
  are not adopted automatically; open them from the session list.
- **`TERM=dumb` and a non-terminal stdin/stdout are refused** with a pointer to print mode
  (`zyris-code -p "…"`), instead of panicking or writing escape codes into a pipe.

Windows now know about each other through a small registry of live instances, and the shared
state they used to race on is coordinated:

- Only one window enrolls; the others wait for its credential instead of timing out and exiting.
- `/undo` refuses to revert a file another live window has edited since, rather than erasing that
  edit.
- Edits to the same file from two windows are serialized, and `git.commit` commits exactly the
  paths it was given, so it no longer sweeps in what another window staged. Concluding a merge,
  cherry-pick or rebase still works.
- Settings files are written atomically, and a setting changed in one window (such as
  `/config dir deny`) reaches the others instead of being written back over.
- The app log is appended to by every window, each line prefixed with `[pid]`. The connection
  failure message says how to read only this run's lines.

## Messages, plans and stuck screens

- A message typed while a turn is running is now sent; it used to be echoed and dropped.
- Approving a plan now actually lets the agent write.
- `/github login` and a question arriving over a form no longer freeze the screen, and the slower
  actions that still wait say "Working…" first. A failed send puts the text back in the draft,
  and messages typed while offline are sent on reconnect.

## Terminals

- Colours follow what the terminal can show (24-bit, 256 or 16), and the background colour is
  asked for, so light themes are readable. `TERM=linux` gets ASCII marks; `ZYRIS_CODE_ASCII`
  forces either way. `NO_COLOR` covers the screen.
- The terminal is restored on every way out: signals before the first connection, a panic, and
  the watchdog. Ctrl+Z suspends and `fg` resumes.
- Ctrl+J inserts a newline on terminals without the kitty keyboard protocol; Ctrl+H is
  Backspace; Tab in the draft inserts spaces. Pastes are normalised (CRLF, tabs, control
  characters).
- Widths are measured by grapheme cluster, the way the screen is drawn. Long lines, URLs, code
  and tables wrap instead of being clipped, and copying them gives the whole text back.
  `ZYRIS_CODE_AMBIGUOUS_WIDE=1` helps terminals that draw East Asian ambiguous characters wide.
- Links open only for `http`, `https` and `mailto`, and the opener no longer inherits the
  terminal.
- Copy reaches the system clipboard over SSH (OSC 52) and inside tmux.
- `ZYRIS_CODE_REDUCE_MOTION` stops the blinking and spinning.

## Measuring what tools cost

Every tool answer's size is now logged, and `scripts/exec_report.py` reports cost per tool,
the largest file reads, and whether a cut `exec` answer was read back.
